messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: no semicolons in probs; no 1-chain examples
parts:
On 4/13/13 9:32 PM, Andrew Gelman wrote:
> Just two very minor things:
>
> On pages 4 and 5, it should be p(theta|y,x), p(y|theta,x), p(theta|x). No semicolons.

I thought we'd gotten rid of all these. I like
the semicolons to distinguish what's being modeled
probabilistically (outcomes y) and what's not (predictors
x), but we'll keep with Andrew's overloaded notation
for "|" to mean conditioning on data or conditional
probabilities.

> Also, in the example on page 12, please run with 4 chains, not 1. I don't want any 1-chain examples, this could mislead
> people!
> Same in Section 4.1. Let's not have any 1-chain examples, please.

The model command only has the capability of running
one chain. So to run four chains, you need to run
one chain four different times.

We can do that.

But what we should do is include a four-chain option
in the model command itself. The big drawback is that
it will run them sequentially rather than in parallel.
We could write scripts for various platforms to kick off
multiple jobs.

- Bob
